claim: Stage ages in Piaget's theory are task-dependent: simpler or better-cued versions of the same tasks are passed years earlier (conservation 6-8y vs teddy version at 4y; policeman doll 90% at 3.5-5y vs mountains 7-8y; object permanence 9 months vs 3.5-5.5 months by looking time).
agent_test: Background only. Vary cue and question format of one reasoning task and check if accuracy shifts as much as model size does.
audit_note: Hughes, McGarrigle and Donaldson, and Rose and Blank are checked only via Wikipedia; Baillargeon 1987 supports 3.5-month success only for fast habituators (4.5-month group overall), and Piaget's 'about 9 months' is from Baillargeon's own summary.

claim: Asking the same conservation question twice, or a loaded question, makes young children change answers; one-question or teddy versions raise success. Task framing, not only capacity, drives the error (Samuel and Bryant n=252 only seen in a snippet). (d14: abstract of Samuel and Bryant 1984 confirms the one-question effect for mass and volume at ages 5-8; exact means and N=252 still second-hand.)
agent_test: Ask the same question once vs repeated in a clarify loop; measure answer flips at equal tokens.
audit_note: Samuel and Bryant 1984 abstract (via Europe PMC) confirms one-question benefit for mass and volume at ages 5-8 and cites Rose and Blank for 6-year-olds; N=252 not verified, already flagged in the claim. 'Loaded question' and teddy version rest on Wikipedia only.

claim: Looking-time evidence for early object permanence (Baillargeon 1987: 4.5m N=24, impossible 29.2s vs possible 17.7s) is contested: Bogartz et al. 2000 show familiarisation trial number flips the direction of looking, an alternative non-knowledge account. Added: Bogartz 2000 N=36 and N=52, possibility parameter p=.92; no multi-lab object-permanence replication found.
agent_test: None needed for agent. Warning that one indirect measure can support two stories.

claim: A-not-B errors depend on delay and cue strength (Clearfield 2009, N=108: cue effect F(2,102)=7.69), and a dynamic model reproduces this, so the error is not a clean stage marker.
agent_test: None.
audit_note: Clearfield 2009 matches (108, F(2,102)=7.69, delay x cue F=3.38) and the authors say the interaction supports the dynamic field account; model fit is their prediction, not a new simulation.

claim: Capacity rises steadily with age from about 2-2.5 chunks in preschoolers to 3-4 in adults, but infant looking tasks suggest about 3, and no decisive experiment separates capacity from attention control or strategy accounts.
agent_test: Hold load constant, vary distractors and filtering; see if failures track capacity or control.

claim: Neo-Piagetian capacity ladders (Halford unary to quaternary, about ages 1,3,5,10; Pascual-Leone 1 to 7 units) are post hoc: the arity assigned to each task is chosen by theorists and binary shortcuts can solve some tasks.
agent_test: Operationalise relational complexity (REL) and test if accuracy falls with it at fixed tokens.

claim: LLM accuracy falls as relational complexity (number of jointly bound relations) rises: Raven items down 45% from RC 3 to 9, phylogeny down 93% from RC 5 to 20, chemistry completion 65.7/38.1/26.0%. But REL-C1 and C2 share RC=2 yet differ 65.7 vs 38.1, so RC is not the only driver. Update: in a controlled biology task RC explains 24-44% of variance (d11); in chemistry operand complexity also matters (C1 65.7 vs C2 38.1 at RC=2).
agent_test: Decompose high-RC items into stepwise binary relations vs direct answer at equal tokens; log RC.

claim: Large VLMs fail conservation tasks: 112 VLMs, 23,040 trials, human 98.35% (6 adults); 82 of 112 (73.2%) under 10% strict pairwise accuracy; only 3 above chance 33.3%. Failure shows as bias toward answering conserve (blank-image conserve 85.7%).
agent_test: Run own agent on a subset with matched control items; always score conserving and non-conserving pairs.

claim: In ConservationBench scale barely helps conservation (R2=0.019 over 1B-76B) and explains under 24% of non-conserving control accuracy (R2=0.239). Correction: b08 reads 0.239 as the general scale effect; it is the control items only.
agent_test: None.

claim: Chain-of-thought hurts on number and length conservation (F(3,333)=18.28, p<.001) and reasoning models show no significant gain in 10 of 12 CoreCognition abilities.
agent_test: Compare direct vs CoT per task type at equal tokens; route perceptual items away from long CoT.
audit_note: Reasoning-vs-instruct result in CoreCognition is about reasoning models, not CoT prompting; ConservationBench CoT effect is for number and length video tasks (F(3,333)=18.28, p<.001), matches.

claim: The 2024 Luo workshop result (5 VLMs, GPT-4o 97.44% transformational vs 31.22% non-transformational, 22.11% number) points the same way as the 2026 112-model study: models do well when the change is shown, poorly when judging static end states. The two studies share authors, so independence is partial.
agent_test: Not directly applicable.
audit_note: Numbers match; the 2024 paper (Luo, Lyu, Gao, Sun, Li, Deng) and the 2026 study (Luo, Li, ..., Deng) share authors, as the claim states; evidence row a22 mislabels the 2024 paper as 'Su et al.'.

claim: CogLM text benchmark: GPT-4 84.7% (age 20.0) vs adult 93.7% (21.5); planning 59.4 vs 95.6 and propositional 61.0 vs 82.0 are the largest gaps. Stage-age mapping is the authors' regression fit and the human sample (141 valid, ages 6-20) is small. Verified against the paper tables.
agent_test: Run planning and propositional subsets with and without an explicit plan step at equal tokens.

claim: On CogLM, CoT and self-consistency did not help GPT-3.5 (64.0 base, 64.3 CoT, 64.4 SC at T0.3, 63.1 at T0.7), while Chain-of-Cognition (prior-stage answers fed in) lifted a small model 31.0 to 38.1.
agent_test: Feed earlier-stage sub-answers into later-stage questions; compare with matched extra tokens of plain CoT.

claim: LLM developmental order is not human: CoreCognition finds lowest-stage perception and perspective taking weak (humans 86.98 vs GPT-4o 69.25; gaps 15.9-22.5 on lower stages) and perspective taking declines with scale; CogDevelop2K reports a reversed pattern.
agent_test: Do not assume a lower-stage skill is mastered; probe it directly.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Concept-explanation or cognitive-instruction prompts add modest gains (CoreCognition over +6%; CogDevelop2K GPT-4o High 0.555 to 0.636).
agent_test: State the governing concept before answering vs no hint, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Models can be steered to mimic age: GPT-4 role-playing children (Milicka 2024, 1,296 trials) downplays its knowledge on false-belief; ChildAgentEval (single study) shows age-label prompts give weak age alignment (Spearman -0.40) while skill-guided prompts reach 1.00.
agent_test: Low priority for agent.

claim: LLMs have strong storage but weak control: operation span 0.92-0.99 vs human 0.53, but flanker incongruent 0.40-0.60 vs 0.93-0.96 and WCST 0.29-0.53 vs 0.77. Reasoning fixes flanker (0.471 to 0.910) but not WCST.
agent_test: Add an explicit conflict-check or switch step on flanker-like and rule-switch items; compare token cost.
audit_note: All numbers (operation span, flanker, WCST, flanker 0.471 to 0.910) come from one paper, de Langis et al. arXiv 2504.02789, listed three times; they match, but the other cited sources (Gong 2023, Huang 2025) do not report these figures. The tested models are open 7-70B models.

claim: Verbal n-back d' drops to about 1 at n=3 for GPT-3.5 (H=58.54, p=1.94e-13); GPT-4 stays above 1 to n=3 (H=52.51); small open models show no n effect. Verified in paper tables.
agent_test: Test n-back style dependency tracking with and without an external scratch list.

claim: Piaget-inspired schema memory helps agents: PISA LOCOMO 63.58 vs Mem0 55.51 (full context 68.47); CAM NovelQA 52.3 vs 47.8. Gains are against specific baselines on own benchmarks, and the Piaget mechanisms themselves were not ablated. Update: ablations exist only for parts. SCG-Mem without assimilation loses 20-35% F1; CAM without hierarchy loses 5.6-11 ACC-L points; PISA ablates init and retrieval only.
agent_test: Ablate schema revision (accommodation-like) in our memory at equal tokens.

claim: ManyBabies-style replication (37 labs, 567 usable infants) tested infant helper preference; evidence (BF01 over 100 with informative prior) favoured no difference between social and nonsocial conditions, against the pattern expected from earlier literature (meta-analysis 0.64 preference). Shows multi-lab work can shift single-lab claims; domain is social, not Piagetian. Reading of b20 is from its abstract-level numbers.
agent_test: None.

claim: A connectionist model of the balance scale task (Schapiro and McClelland 2009) reproduces the Rule I to Rule II transition and the 'catastrophe flags' seen in Jansen and van der Maas's child data, and accounts for nearly all of it with continuous processes, consistent with the transition being typically continuous rather than discrete; a cascade-correlation network (Shultz 1996) reproduces five conservation phenomena.
agent_test: None; background.
audit_note: Schapiro and McClelland model only the Rule I to Rule II transition and conclude it is typically continuous rather than discrete (a few children show larger jumps than the model); Shultz 1996 abstract lists five conservation phenomena and does not mention stage-like jumps. The N=314 and 2-8% flag percentages could not be re-read (PDF unreachable).
claim_before_audit: Connectionist and constructive networks reproduce stage-like jumps and balance-scale rule sequences, supporting a continuous-learning account of stages (child data N=314, catastrophe flags 2-8%).

claim: Text-only and blank-image controls show the VLM conservation failure is mostly a response bias to answer Conserve, not a pure perceptual deficit. Blank image 85.7% Conserve, text-only 73.7%, real images about 60%; an I-dont-know option did not remove it.
agent_test: Give a reasoning agent balanced conserve and change items with and without the evidence; measure the share that answer Conserve blind.

claim: Decomposition-first prompting (least-to-most) beats plain CoT where problems exceed demo length: SCAN length split 99.7 vs 16.2, DROP football 73.42 vs 59.56; on GSM8K only 62.39 vs 60.87. No equal-token test on a modern reasoning model exists.
agent_test: Same token budget: prerequisite sub-answers first vs one long CoT, on a strong reasoning model.

claim: Reasoning traces fix flanker-type interference (Llama-8B 0.471 to 0.910) but not rule switching (WCST 0.29-0.53 vs adults 0.77, no gain from reasoning even with hints). Cost is thousands of tokens.
agent_test: Add an explicit current-rule register to the scaffold; test on WCST-style tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Relational complexity predicts LLM errors when other factors are held fixed: biology B1 accuracy 35% at 4 taxa to 1% at 25, RC explaining 24-44% of explainable variance; test-time compute and tools do not lift it.
agent_test: Hold object count fixed; vary only binding load per step.

claim: In SCG-Mem, disabling assimilation (keeping only accommodation) lowers F1 by 20.1-34.8% on Qwen2.5-3B; CAM without hierarchy loses 5.3-11.0 ACC-L points (NovelQA 5.6, QMSum 11.0, ODSum-S 5.3). PISA ablates only its initialization module and hierarchy-aware retrieval, with no ablation of its Piagetian update, and assimilation-only (without accommodation) is untested in SCG-Mem.
schema_part: O (revise schema only after assimilation fails)
agent_test: Run an assimilate-first vs always-write memory arm in the scaffold.
audit_note: SCG-Mem's 'w/o Evolutionary Update' removes assimilation and retains only accommodation, so accommodation-alone is effectively tested (it is assimilation-alone that is untested); SCG-Mem ablation is on one model (Qwen2.5-3B), F1 drops 20.1-34.8%; CAM w/o Hierarchy drop on ODSum-S is 5.3 not 5.6, so the range is 5.3-11.0.
claim_before_audit: Schema-grounded memory ablations: removing assimilation drops SCG-Mem F1 by 20-35% on 3B models; CAM without hierarchy loses 5.6-11 ACC-L points. Accommodation alone and the Piagetian update in PISA have no ablation.

claim: False-belief accuracy of LLMs depends on prompt framing: CoT helps clean items (+22.4) but hardly perturbed ones (+3.9) and hurts some (-12.1). Reasoning-trained models were excluded, so newer-model behaviour is untested.
agent_test: Evaluate the scaffold on perturbed, not classic, social-reasoning items.

claim: Infant false-belief looking-time and interactive tasks mostly fail to replicate (Powell 2018: 21.0 vs 18.3 s, P>0.1; Wenzel 2020 chance in 48+48 children). No multi-lab object-permanence replication was found.
agent_test: Do not anchor design on infant competence claims.
audit_note: Powell 2018 (violation-of-expectation false-belief task, 21.0 vs 18.3 s, P>0.1) matches; Wenzel 2020 abstract reports failure to replicate Sefo in 17-month-olds and 3-year-olds (48 per group inferred from n); note in Wenzel a pooled 3-year-old FB check was significant (p=.05), and Powell had other tasks that did replicate, so 'mostly' is fair.
